current_activity: arrives by rail at Sarrebourg, scattered by an air attack while entrained, and reorganizes for the march west
notes: Event date: 16 September 1944 (Wikipedia; Cole, ch. 5). Event definition: Sent from Colmar to Sarrebourg on 16 September (Wikipedia); east of Sarrebourg part of the brigade is reorganized for the march west after an air attack scattered it while still entrained; the same day OB West assigns it to the LVIII Panzer Corps (Cole, ch. 5). Event support: two source families (the US Army official history (CMH), and Wikipedia). Cole, The Lorraine Campaign, ch. 5, p. 218: "part of the 113th Panzer Brigade was being reorganized for the march west"; Cole, The Lorraine Campaign, ch. 5, p. 218: "The LVIII Panzer Corps, on the right, was assigned the 113th Panzer Brigade"; Wikipedia, 113th Panzer Brigade: "on 16 September sent to Saarburg". Location: Sarrebourg, Moselle (new place) with a precision of 5 km. Location support: Wikipedia and Cole name Sarrebourg (Saarburg). Commander: Colonel Erich Freiherr von Seckendorff (Cole, ch. 5, n. 32; Wikipedia).

current_activity: forty-two Panthers attack in fog from Bourdonnay via Ley toward Bezange and run into CCA, 4th Armored Division
notes: Event date: 19 September 1944, from about 0800 (Cole, ch. 5; Wikipedia). Event definition: After a night march from Bourdonnay the brigade, with forty-two Panthers and the 2113th Panzer Grenadier Regiment in the lead, reorganizes near Ley and pushes through heavy fog toward Bezange; in the meeting engagement with CCA it attacks in consecutive jabs and loses heavily (Cole, ch. 5; Wikipedia, Battle of Arracourt). Event support: two source families (the US Army official history (CMH), and Wikipedia). Cole, The Lorraine Campaign, ch. 5, p. 224: "had moved from Bourdonnay in a successful night march, reorganized its advance guard near Ley, and now pushed through the heavy fog toward Bezange"; Wikipedia, Battle of Arracourt: "At 08:00 on 19 September, company-sized elements of the 113th Panzer Brigade penetrated CCA outposts". Location: Bezange-la-Petite, Moselle (new place) with a precision of 3 km. Location support: Cole names Bourdonnay, Ley and Bezange. Commander: Colonel Erich Freiherr von Seckendorff (Cole, ch. 5, n. 32; Wikipedia). Opponents: US 4th Armored Division (CCA). Context: The Bezange named by Cole is taken as Bezange-la-Petite, on the road from Ley toward Arracourt (inferred value).

location_qualifier: two battalions of the 113th Panzer Grenadier Regiment
current_activity: two battalions of its 113th Panzer Grenadier Regiment counterattack the 79th Division in the Forêt de Parroy
notes: Event date: 1 October 1944 (Clarke and Smith, ch. 14). Event definition: On 1 October the LVIII Panzer Corps sends two battalions of the brigade's panzer grenadier regiment, with more armour, into the Forêt de Parroy against the 79th Infantry Division; the hard-hit brigade is incorporated into the 15th Panzer Grenadier Division the same day (Clarke and Smith, ch. 14; Wikipedia). Event support: two source families (the US Army official history (CMH), and Wikipedia). Clarke and Smith, Riviera to the Rhine, ch. 14, p. 267: "The LVIII Panzer Corps deployed two battalions of the 113th Panzer Grenadier Regiment, 113th Panzer Brigade, into the forest"; Wikipedia, 113th Panzer Brigade: "On 1 October 1944, the 113th Panzer Brigade was disbanded". Location: Forêt de Parroy, Meurthe-et-Moselle with a precision of 5 km. Location support: Clarke and Smith name the Parroy forest. Opponents: US 79th Infantry Division. Context: Commander: Seckendorff was killed on 23 September (Cole, ch. 5, n. 32); his successor is not named in the sources read.
